newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond issues line up to come to market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond issues line up to come to market.

text.p: An unofficial calendar for new corporate bond issues continues to build, dealers said, as opportunistic issuers including a unit of GTE Corp, prepare to tap the market on any dips in U.S. Treasury yields.
"There's a lot of names in the market," said one syndicate source. "Everyone's just waiting for them to price."
A number of debt offerings are lined up to come to market near-term, dealers said, but no official dates have been set.
GTE Hawaiin Telephone Co is expected to price $150 million in 10-year debentures via competitive bid as early as Tuesday, sources said.
Signet Bank is expected to price $150 million in Baa1/BBB-minus rated 10-year subordinated notes via JP Morgan Securities, one day this week.
Among other banks expected to tap the primary market are this week are Wells Fargo, NationsBank, and Key Bank dealers added.

In the private placement sector, United USN Inc is expected to set $155 million in eight-year 144A senior notes this week, and First Nationwide Holdings is expected to price $525 million in seven-year senior subordinated 144A notes via Smith Barney.
Turning to yankee offerings, Australia & New Zealand Banking Group is expected to price up to $500 million in 10-year yankee subordinated debt via Merrill Lynch & Co.
Also, European Investment Bank is expected to price between $1.0 to $1.5 billion in 10-year global bonds via joint managers CS First Boston and Lehman Brothers.
In addtiion, Argentaria Bank is also expected to tap the market with a $250 million yankee offering, sources said.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond is off 10/32 at 95-22/32 to yield 7.10 percent.
